title: Repository and version control concepts
learningObjectives: Explain repository and version control concepts and use browser or version-control tools to diagnose and publish reliable web projects.

understand.concept: A repository stores project files and version history. Version control records changes over time so teams can compare, restore, branch, and collaborate. A remote repository provides a shared hosted copy of that history.
understand.whyItMatters: Version control protects work and makes changes traceable. It is not a replacement for backups, access control, or release testing.
understand.analogy: A repository is a project's history book, not merely a folder of current files.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; actual developer tools, Git behaviour, and deployment requirements depend on the browser, repository, and hosting provider.

explain.narrative: The list names core repository concepts. Git commands and a hosted platform provide the actual operations.

examples.explanation: The list names core repository concepts. Git commands and a hosted platform provide the actual operations.
examples.expectedOutput: The example illustrates the workflow or developer-tool concept; command examples require a practice repository.

practise.guidedTask: Create a local repository, inspect its status and history, and explain the difference between local and remote copies.
practise.independentTask: Apply the workflow to a small static site. Capture the commands or browser evidence, identify risks, and document recovery steps.
hints: Inspect actual files and browser behaviour.
Do not commit secrets or personal data.
Verify provider-specific deployment values before changing DNS.
